title: Statistical Screening for Poisoned Machine-Learning Training Data
subtitle: Detection and Quarantine of Suspicious Samples at the Data-Ingestion Boundary
contribution: An ingestion-boundary screening pipeline combining statistical outlier methods with a label-aware cross-class centroid detector that improves the committed synthetic label-flip benchmark from the old top-1 spectral baseline 0.08 / 0.23 / 0.3675 F1 to 0.55 / 0.595 / 0.6975 F1 at 5% / 10% / 20% contamination.
methods: Validate incoming feature batches and streaming samples.
Apply z-score, IQR, Isolation Forest, and spectral/label-aware detectors.
Combine detector signals for screening and quarantine workflows.
Maintain streaming state and deduplication metadata.
Benchmark label-flip behavior with committed reproducible artifacts.
evidence: Cited Python 3.12 CI: 200 passed; 91.20% statement coverage, same test job.
Committed synthetic experiment: 2,000 samples, 100 features, class separation 2.0, seed 2018; not production data.
At 5/10/20% random class-0-to-class-1 label flips, centroid F1 = 0.55/0.595/0.6975; old top-1 spectral F1 = 0.08/0.23/0.3675; ensemble F1 = 0.0841/0.1421/0.2331.
Result source: results/spectral_benchmark.json. Recorded artifact values were checked; no new population efficacy estimate is made.
limitations: The benchmark is synthetic and separable; it is not proof of production detection rate.
Clean-label, subtle backdoor, and very-low-rate poisoning remain difficult.
Throughput is hardware/environment dependent; no fixed product SLA is claimed.
Stateful streaming behavior requires deliberate partitioning/external state for horizontal scaling.
reproduction: Install the documented development dependencies; run python -m pytest tests/ -q. Use the cited job configuration when reproducing coverage.
Benchmark data, adapters and environment requirements are separate; consult poster/13_reproducibility.md and the claim ledger.
